Popovac Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Popovac, Croatia

Not demolished. Popovača developed as a fortress town and regional trading center in the Middle Ages, its population fleeing during the 16th-century Ottoman threat before flourishing again afterward as a weekly fair center; a 19th-century railway line further boosted its economy. Jews first settled in the town in the 19th century, maintaining a synagogue and this cemetery, closely connected to the Jewish community of Kutina, documented elsewhere in this collection. Before WWII, only 8 Jews lived in Popovača; none remained afterward.
